results.name: Model 47A - Loggerhead Sea Turtle
results.description:
This is a 3D animation ("Shelly") of a near-adult loggerhead (ID=982.000406129037) sea turtle (*Caretta caretta*, straight carapace length=86 cm) that was initially captured on June 23, 2017 by the Inwater Research Group, and then photgraphed with the Beastcam technology with 20 Canon G16 cameras.  Photographer Christine Shepard operated the cameras and the sea turtle was released that same day in good condition.  The 3D model was initially created through a photogrammetry scan using Capturing Reality.

Animator Johnson Martin  used Blender to reconstruct the full sea turtle from these scans, as well as animate the movements. Jeanette Wyneken from Florida Atlantic University, and Charles Mairne from the Loggerhead MarineLife Center each provided feedback on the movements.

If you are interested in downloading this 3D model, please visit our website www.digitallife3d.org

results.name: Kokura Castle
results.description:
This 3D data of Kokura Castle was made using photogrammetry. This is Avatta's first attempt in using drones to make high quality 3D architectural scan. We have photographed over 1500 images from all directions and the data was processed using Agisoft Photoscan. 

Kokura Castle of Kitakyushu, Japan was built by Hosokawa Tadaoki in 1602. It was the property of the Ogasawara clan (from Harima) between 1632 and 1860. The castle was burnt down in 1866 in the war between the Kokura and Chōshū clans.

Mori Ogai was based at the castle at the turn of the 19th-20th century when it was a military base.
The keep was reconstructed in 1959, and the castle was fully restored in 1990. The Matsumoto Seicho museum and castle garden were opened in 1998. The old Japanese-style pre-Brunton lighthouse from Shirasu is in the castle grounds.

results.name: Affinis Snyders Arrowhead (in-situ 3D scan!)
results.description:
This is my first attempt at 3D scanning an artifact as found, using 29 photos (overhead grid pattern) in 3df zephyr free.  It was right before sunset, so the lighting wasn't great, and that made the flaking pattern really hard to see in the model.  However, the side that was facing down has some really impressive flaking!  
The right side is partially missing, as is the better part of the left ear...  that makes it really hard to identify.  The closest type I could find is Affinis Snyders.  
The material is a white flint, spattered with iron deposits.
Oh... and in case you were wondering what the green stuff is, those were soybean plants.  turns out zephyr couldn't do much with them (I'm not a great photographer), so it just pasted them over everything else.
Collection id: p68.

results.name: Losey Gravestone - 4K Video Test Scan
results.description: This is a test scan of the Losey Gravestone in the Oak Grove Cemetery, La Crosse, Wisconsin.  It was scanned using a 2 min 46 sec 4K video shot with a Motorola Moto G5 Plus mobile phone camera and a Zhiyun Smooth-Q stablizing gimble.  Every 45th frame was extracted from the video (i.e. every 1.5 seconds) for a total of 110 frames utilized to generate the scan using Agisoft Metashape 1.5.5. Frame extraction was performed using Metashape's video import function. The focus of the scanning was on the inscription, so the top of the stone was not adequetly "photographed" and has been retouched using Meshmixer 3.5.  No other parts of the stone have been retouched or modified from that which was generated by Metashape.

results.name: Crippling
results.description:
Yet another Work In Progress that I'll left "unprogressed on", as a by-product of my latest Blender/Sketchfab experiments.

* High-resolution hand scan: ["Hand"](https://skfb.ly/6GW88) by @artec3d, CC-attribution. 
* Base hand mesh used for the retopology: [Low Poly Human Hands (All Quads)](https://skfb.ly/6NUy9) from @JeremyGrayson, CC-Attribution.
* Eye: [Blue Eyeball (Free)](https://skfb.ly/6HUzo) from @tomhodes, CC-Attribution.
* Base face mesh: "Female Base Mesh" from [Javier Zuccarino](https://www.artstation.com/zuka) (who shared it for free on his Gumroad profile: "Zucca")
* [Initial face texture](https://bit.ly/32r2bl8) from "The Internet", a.k.a. sorry I did not manage to trace it back to the photographer :(

This model is left unfinished and most noticeably some of the hands are not posed by simple lack of patience, but I did not feel like I was really going anywhere with this scene.

Note to self: think about finishing something someday !

results.description:
This is a 3D model (“Tumbleweed”) of a juvenile Kemps Ridley Sea Turtle (ID 132) (*Lepidochelys kempii*) that was initially rescued by the New England Aquarium in Massachusetts, and then photographed with the Beastcam technology with 30 Canon G16 cameras.
